headline: Low interaction risk overall; no shared channels or write surfaces are documented, so prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors are not evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Neither profile documents a shared communication channel, filesystem bridge, or parser relationship. Agent A is non-runnable with network egress none, and agent B exposes no I/O surfaces or capabilities. With no documented path for A’s outputs to reach B as instructions, prompt injection is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the agents, reassess injection risk.
IF agent B begins parsing agent A’s text as instructions, the pathway becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any copy-paste or shared clipboard bridge.
Do not route A’s outputs into B as executable prompts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: No shared workspace, filesystem, OAuth principal, or outbound network path is documented for either agent. Agent A has network egress none, and agent B lists no capabilities or I/O surfaces. Without a data path, there is no plausible leakage route between them in the documented configuration.
conditions: IF both agents are mounted on the same shared workspace, leakage risk must be re-evaluated.
IF either agent is given file-upload or network-send capability, leakage becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared directory.
Run each agent under a separate OS account.
Avoid mounting the same workspace into both agents.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls if sharing is needed.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Capability overlap is not documented: agent A has only network_egress none, while agent B has an empty capabilities block and no concurrency model. There is no evidence of shared write access, git state, or mutable resource coordination, so a write conflict pathway is not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or repo, conflict risk becomes relevant.
IF either agent gains mutable OAuth or database scopes, reassess overlap.
mitigations: Do not grant shared write permissions.
Separate any mutable resources by agent.
Use a single writer for each repo or directory.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutation is unavoidable.

D_cascading_error.rationale: The profiles do not show a pipeline where B consumes A’s outputs as authoritative input, nor any downstream action-taking authority. Agent A is a non-runnable awesome-list repo and agent B is a content-writing repo with no documented execution surfaces, so a cascading error chain is not evidenced.
conditions: IF B is configured to ingest A’s text as source-of-truth without review, cascading error risk appears.
IF either agent is connected to an action channel such as email, commits, or tickets, reassess impact.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before reuse of outputs.
Require source citations for any copied claims.
Keep A and B in separate stages with explicit validation.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: No regulated data class, residency constraint, retention policy, or certification mismatch is documented for either agent. Agent A touches no data classes and agent B also lists no data classes touched, so there is no compliance pathway to evaluate from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned regulated data such as PHI or EU PII, compliance must be re-evaluated.
IF retention or residency policies diverge for a shared data class, reassess.
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through either agent.
Document data-class handling before deployment.
Keep retention settings aligned across tools.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated workloads.
